content: If I get a second Bachelor's degree am I eligible for another round of OPT?

<response>
Based on the information provided, if you receive a second Bachelor's degree, you are indeed eligible for another round of OPT. The key point here is that the degree must be from an accredited U.S. college or university, and the OPT employment opportunity must be directly related to the degree field. It's important to note that you can only receive a total of two lifetime STEM OPT extensions, and these extensions must be based on different degrees. If you've already received a STEM OPT extension based on a previous degree, you can still apply for another OPT extension based on your new Bachelor's degree, as long as it meets the eligibility criteria and you haven't exceeded the total lifetime limit of two STEM OPT extensions.

Before applying, ensure that you've completed all course requirements for your Bachelor's degree (excluding thesis or equivalent) and that the degree is in a STEM field that appears on the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List at the time of your DSO's recommendation. Additionally, you must follow the guidelines for OPT eligibility, including having been in the United States and in F-1 visa status for at least one academic year or will complete one year by the time OPT approval begins, and not having been authorized for a total of 12 months of Curricular Practical Training (CPT).

Lastly, remember to apply for OPT as early as possible to avoid delays. You can apply up to 90 days before your degree completion, but no later than 60 days after your degree completion. Make sure to check the latest guidelines and requirements from USCIS and your school's International Student Office for any updates or changes.

If you have any specific questions or need further clarification, feel free to ask!
</response>
